published_prior_art.cite: KairouzOhViswanath2016 supplies staircase geometry for convex/sublinear privacy utilities, not the composite exact-confidence decision game.
Mai2023 supplies generic Fritz-John polynomial-optimization machinery, not this common-channel exact-confidence lifting or equality set.
GhaziNasserCalmonIssa2026 treats two-known-distribution f-divergence testing, not a schedulewise composite-confidence loss.
Mai2023 gives generic finite-convergence conditions, not a primal-dual privacy-channel active-set certificate for this game.
ChenCormodeBharadwajRomovOzgur2024 studies distributed-DP ATE design and CI width, not an exact hidden-assignment local-channel phase boundary.
RigdonHudgens2015 supplies the nonprivate exact binary-outcome randomization-inference endpoint.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves staircase optimality for sublinear utilities and a finite LP formulation; its general bounded-output argument is for convex utilities, not the proposal's optimized composite confidence value.
The paper develops locally private causal estimators, variance estimators, plug-in confidence intervals, and minimax-MSE results for randomized experiments.
The paper gives two exact randomization-based confidence-set constructions for a binary-outcome average treatment effect without superpopulation sampling assumptions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1080 abstract; pp. 1080--1081, Introduction and Section 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies minimax expected-size confidence regions for a fixed statistical experiment and randomized confidence actions via least-favorable-prior methods.
The paper formulates ATE experiment design under distributed DP, explicitly distinguishes that model from local DP, and analyzes asymptotic and nonasymptotic CI width.
The paper establishes finite convergence of Fritz-John-strengthened moment-SOS relaxations under stated critical-value/minimizer conditions.
The paper proves sort-partition-randomize structure for f-divergence binary hypothesis testing between two known distributions under pure LDP.
